boards.title: Your First Weekend at The University of Texas at Austin, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A campus-centered, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented through documented UT Austin destinations, public art, study space, and cultural stops.

cards.title: Start at the Tower
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · orient on the Forty Acres
cards.notes: Use the Tower as your visual anchor, then pause at the Main Building plaza to get your bearings before choosing the next stop.
cards.short_summary: Begin with UT Austin’s most recognizable campus landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Austin identifies the Tower as its most recognizable landmark and symbol.
cards.source_title: Campus Destinations | The University of Texas at Austin
cards.access_notes: Enjoy the exterior and plaza; this card does not assume access to the building or observation deck.

cards.title: Pick Up Local Orientation Material
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Texas Union, South Lobby
cards.notes: Stop at the Hospitality Center for campus and Austin information, then use its pamphlets and bus schedules to shape the rest of your weekend.
cards.short_summary: A staffed information stop inside UT’s historic student union.
cards.evidence_claim: The Texas Union Hospitality Center provides answers about the Unions, UT Austin, and Austin, plus free informational pamphlets and bus schedules.
cards.access_notes: The Hospitality Center is in the Texas Union South Lobby during building hours; verify the day’s hours before going.

cards.title: Make a Low-Key Group Plan
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Texas Union
cards.notes: Meet up at the Underground and choose a shared activity such as bowling, billiards, or games; check current availability before committing.
cards.short_summary: An indoor Texas Union activity space with games and bowling.
cards.evidence_claim: UT’s Texas Union lists the Underground as offering bowling, billiards, games, and more.
cards.access_notes: Activities may require payment or availability; confirm details onsite or through University Unions.

cards.title: Take the PCL Self-Guided Tour
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 101 E. 21st Street
cards.notes: Use the library’s self-guided tour to locate study floors, help desks, and practical services you may want during your first weeks.
cards.short_summary: Learn the layout of UT Austin’s flagship research library.
cards.evidence_claim: Perry-Castañeda Library is UT Austin’s flagship research library and offers a self-guided tour.
cards.source_title: Perry-Castañeda Library | University of Texas Libraries
cards.access_notes: The library serves campus communities and the greater public; access is limited to current UT ID holders from 8 p.m. to 7 a.m.

cards.title: Browse the Map Collection
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Perry-Castañeda Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Head to Floor 1 and look through the map collection as a tactile way to learn Austin and identify neighborhoods for a future daytime outing.
cards.short_summary: A map-focused stop inside PCL’s six-level building.
cards.evidence_claim: PCL’s floor plan places the Map Collection on Floor 1, and PCL describes the collection as holding more than 250,000 maps.
cards.source_title: Perry-Castañeda Library Floor Plan | University of Texas Libraries
cards.access_notes: Enter PCL from its southwest-corner plaza at Speedway and 21st Street; follow library guidance for collection use.

cards.title: Walk to the Canoe Sculpture
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · northwest corner of 24th Street and Speedway
cards.notes: Walk over in daylight, look at the suspended boats from more than one angle, and use the official audio guide if you want added context.
cards.short_summary: A 2015 Landmarks sculpture made from 70 aluminum boats and canoes.
cards.evidence_claim: Landmarks identifies Monochrome for Austin as a 2015 UT Austin commission at 24th Street and Speedway, made from 70 aluminum boats and canoes.
cards.access_notes: It is an outdoor public-art work. Landmarks states that outdoor public art is viewable at all times.

cards.title: Continue the Public-Art Walk
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Speedway entrance to GDC
cards.notes: Continue south on Speedway to compare the low circular concrete work with the larger sculpture you just visited; keep the route pedestrian-focused.
cards.short_summary: A Sol LeWitt outdoor work at the Gates Dell Complex entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Landmarks places Sol LeWitt’s Circle with Towers at the Speedway entrance to the Bill & Melinda Gates Computer Science Complex and Dell Computer Science Hall.
cards.access_notes: Landmarks states that outdoor public art is available for viewing at all times; stay on pedestrian routes around the complex.

cards.title: Choose a Museum Stop
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · UT campus
cards.notes: Check the museum’s current visitor information, then select an exhibition or gallery visit that fits your group’s pace and available time.
cards.short_summary: UT Austin’s university art museum and a documented campus destination.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Austin describes the Blanton Museum of Art as a university art museum with the largest and most comprehensive art collection in Central Texas.
cards.source_title: Campus Destinations | The University of Texas at Austin
cards.access_notes: Confirm current galleries, visitor policies, and admission details directly with the museum before visiting.

cards.title: See What Is on View at the Ransom Center
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · corner of 21st and Guadalupe
cards.notes: Review the current exhibition calendar before heading over, then leave time to look closely at one exhibition rather than rushing through several.
cards.short_summary: A UT Austin humanities research center with public exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harry Ransom Center’s program calendar identifies its location at the corner of 21st and Guadalupe on the UT Austin campus and states that gallery admission is free.
cards.access_notes: The cited calendar lists galleries Tuesday–Friday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; verify current hours and exhibitions before a weekend visit.

cards.title: End with a History-Focused Visit
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · UT Austin campus
cards.notes: Use the final stop for a slower museum visit, reviewing current exhibits and visitor details before you go so the plan matches the day’s schedule.
cards.short_summary: A presidential library and museum on the UT Austin campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Austin describes the LBJ Library as an iconic presidential library and museum covering Lyndon Baines Johnson’s political career and American history.
cards.source_title: Campus Destinations | The University of Texas at Austin
cards.access_notes: Confirm current museum hours, tickets, and entry procedures directly with the LBJ Library before visiting.
